title: Asset Depletion Mortgage in SC: Qualify on Your Retirement
description: How an asset depletion mortgage turns retirement savings into qualifying income, which accounts count under Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, and other SC options.
h1: Can You Get a Mortgage Using Your Assets Instead of Income?

faq.q: How is asset depletion income calculated?
faq.a: Under Fannie Mae's rule, the lender adds your eligible retirement assets, subtracts any withdrawal penalty and the cash used to buy, and divides the rest by the number of months in the loan. On a 30-year loan, $350,000 left over gives $972.22 a month of qualifying income.

faq.q: Can retirees get a mortgage with no income?
faq.a: Often, yes. A lender can turn retirement savings into qualifying income with an asset depletion calculation, with no job required. Social Security and pension income are added to it.

faq.q: Which assets count for an asset depletion mortgage?
faq.a: Under Fannie Mae's rule: 401(k), IRA, SEP and Keogh accounts you can withdraw from freely, and lump-sum retirement or severance payouts. Inheritance, real estate sale proceeds, stock options, lawsuit or lottery money and cryptocurrency do not count.

faq.q: Can I use asset depletion to buy an investment property?
faq.a: Not under Fannie Mae's rule, which allows only a home you live in or a second home. For a rental, a DSCR loan qualifies you on the property's rent instead.

faq.q: Does my age matter for an asset depletion loan?
faq.a: Yes. Fannie Mae allows a larger loan when the owner of the assets is 62 or older at closing. No minimum age is required to use the rule.

faq.q: Do I have to withdraw the money to qualify?
faq.a: No. The lender only has to see that you have the right to withdraw it. The calculation treats the money as income spread over the loan term.
